target_customer: Software engineering teams of 10 or more developers that invest in technical design processes (per the YC page); later positioning on the company site targets teams deploying AI agents.
problem: Designing the systems that integrate AI-generated code is the most manual part of software engineering. The first product, Glide, was an AI editor for technical design docs connected to the codebase.
business_model: B2B SaaS for engineering teams; pricing not found
product_category: Developer tools, AI design docs, later a context engine for AI agent deployments

founders.name: Maksim Ivanov
founders.background_notes: YC page says he was previously at hedge funds and did ML research, without naming employers. The launch post says the team experienced the problem at companies like Bridgewater and SpaceX, but does not say which person worked where. The YC page lists a second team member, Rob, as a contact without a title, so he is not recorded as a co-founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: A small team had to connect a doc editor to a codebase and use LLMs to draft and reason about designs. Standard LLM application engineering with some hard retrieval parts in early 2024.

defensibility.rationale: The product was a thin workflow layer on foundation models in a period when coding assistants were adding planning features, so it was copyable in weeks.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The sources opened do not show any incumbent copying or buying the product. The company later reframed itself as a context engine for AI agents according to its own site.

market_need_then: The YC page says developers had plenty of tools for generating code but none for system design. Demand evidence beyond the founders' claim was not found.

branding.domain_note: Uses agenticlabs.com, the exact name plus .com; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: not described in any source opened
identity.voice_and_tone: Mission statement on site: enable AI systems to grow, adapt and evolve.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic company name using a term that many companies adopted; the product name Glide collides with the better known Glide no-code platform, which appeared in search results for this company.

pivots.from: AI editor for technical design docs (Glide)
pivots.to: Context engine for AI agent deployments (Glide)
pivots.why: Not stated. The current company site describes the context engine while the YC page still describes the design doc editor; the date of the change is unknown.

outcome_analysis: The company is active with a team of two and no public traction numbers. It launched Glide on Hacker News in March 2024 as a design doc editor, then its own site repositioned the product as a context engine for AI agents, which suggests a pivot toward the agent infrastructure wave. Funding is only visible through aggregators, so success or stall cannot be judged from the sources found.
notes: Funding is unverified: aggregators give $125K seed (Signalbase), $500K pre-seed in Apr 2024 (VCBacked) and $500K over 3 rounds (CB Insights), with investors named as Y Combinator, Pioneer Fund, Liquid 2 Ventures, Rebel Fund. The company site shows logos for SVA, General Catalyst and Rebel Fund as backers without amounts. None of these were confirmed by a press release or filing, so no round is recorded. CB Insights fetch was blocked by a rate limit. No dated competitor sources near March 2024 were found. Completeness pass: the 500K pre-seed rests on a single database (VCBacked, April 2024). CB Insights dates a seed to 2024-03-18 with 500K over 3 rounds and different investors (Pioneer Fund, Transpose Platform, Rebel Fund, Maiora Ventures); Signalbase reports 125K. Conflicts unresolved and not summed.
